newsitem.title: USA: US to sell up to 15 mln barrels light sour SPR oil.
newsitem.headline: US to sell up to 15 mln barrels light sour SPR oil.

text.p: The U.S. Energy Department plans to offer up to 15 million barrels of light sour crude from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve in the latest sale ordered by Congress to help close the budget gap, an Energy Department official said.
The first deadline for bids will be October 21, if the department's sales agent, the Defense Fuel Supply Center, gets a request for bids out Thursday or Friday as planned, the official said.
"Right now it is our intent to get the solicitation out tomorrow," he said.

Congress required the Energy Department to sell $220 million worth of oil from the nation's emergency stockpile to cover the costs of maintaining and operating the reserve in the 1997 fiscal year, which began October 1.
The crude for the sale -- the third budget-balancing sale required by Congress since January -- will come from the West Hackberry SPR site in Louisiana.
The oil has a gravity of 33.7 degrees API on average and a sulfur content of 1.44 percent by weight, lighter than the crude sold earlier this year.
"It's similar to Saudi Light," the official said.
The government will also offer 370,000 barrels of West Hackberry sweet crude which is currently being used as pipeline fill.
Deliveries can be made by pipeline or tanker at the Sun Terminal at Nederland, Texas, or to the Texas Pipeline, a common carrier, at Lake Charles, Louisiana.
If first bids come in on October 21, "we can make the first awards later that week if the bids are in line with prevailing market prices," the department official said.
The auction will continue until the government raises the required $220 million.
"We anticipate calling for a new round of bids every two weeks," the official said.
